survive.title: Survive
bullets: Hunger, thirst, energy, and infection tick with every hour. Keep them up — empty hunger or thirst below 35 starts eating limb HP.
Health is the sum of your six limbs — see the Body topic for how each injury changes travel, aim, and stamina. Major bleeds block regen until bandaged; infection at 100 ends the run.
Before a run, pick a job seed or build traits on the same screen — negatives earn points, positives spend them. A full signature + curse spends the whole pool; swap to free a point for another trait.
Night (after dusk) is more dangerous. Get inside before dark — the streets fill with a night swarm. Rest shows recovery and ambush chance; sleep still drains hunger and thirst (reduced).
Hazard pockets sit between pins (horde, patrols, collapse, flood). Sense them inside your ring, route around when you can — each kind bites differently if you cross.

The horde meter is the island clock, not the street under your feet. It climbs every day and every neighbourhood gets worse with it — but a Stirring town is not a Lost one. Ground zero is already Fallen or worse when you wake; distant estates may still be holding. Lost streets stay walkable, they just cost more: denser pockets, dusk-rate swarms in daylight, harder searches. Zoom out until the island fits and the map becomes a status overlay; street zoom stays clear. At 100% the city is overrun and the run ends.
Infected animals share the combat loop and can infect on a hit. Otters and monitors claim inland water, macaques and boars the catchment, dogs/cats/rats the streets.
Fights run on a shared track — whoever fills it swings. Light weapons and a free off-hand fill faster; a shield or a second blade is a real choice.

body.title: Body
bullets: Six limbs share one health pool. A hit lands on a part — bandage bleeds, splint fractures, and don't let a limb hit zero untreated (crippled heals only up to 70%).
Bad legs slow travel on the map. One wrecked leg is a limp; both wrecked is a crawl. Legs do not throttle how fast you fill the combat gauge.
Right arm is your weapon arm (accuracy). Left arm is guard — shields and a free off-hand lose tempo when it's mauled.
Head wounds tax aim, rummage speed, and awareness. Torso wounds raise energy drain and cut how much you can carry.
Open Condition anytime for the body doll. The first time you're hurt, a short coach points you there.

fight.title: Fight
bullets: Both markers race one track. First to the end swings. Speed is how fast you fill it — stance, weapon weight, and a free off-hand all count. Switch Aggressive / Guarded / Precision any time; Break off is the flee.

Holster a pistol or shotgun to shoot — Fire is a separate gauge from melee. Empty + Fire reloads from a loaded magazine (pistol) or 12g shells in pack (shotgun). Wield the gun in main hand to bash; gunshots on the surface draw danger.
Out of combat: right-click a magazine + ammo box to refill, then load it into the holstered pistol. Shotguns take shells directly on the holstered gun. Typed ammo only — no global round pool.

loot.title: Loot
bullets: At a place, start a search: a fogged grid reveals finds one by one in real time. Street sites usually turn up a handful of items — condition tracks how wrecked the place looks.

First visit sizes up the footprint and ruin (Intact → Gutted). Ruin sets the condition band: Intact is Brand New, Damaged is Slightly Used, Ravaged is Heavily Used, Gutted is Old & Torn. A hot site does not turn junk into mint gear.
Click a fogged cell to search it next. Click found items (or Take all) into your pack; overflow goes to the tiny on-site stash (3×3).
Equipped bags change the pack's cell shape, not just its size — holes cannot hold loot. A smaller or hole-punched bag only equips if the current haul can be rearranged into it.
Worn kit counts toward load. Hover the carry bar — a heavy pack never stops a pickup, it just makes travel, fights, and searches cost more.
Each site has limited searches. Leaving early still spends a partial charge. Take what you want — Done or Leave abandons the rest.
Map notes turn up in searches — decipher them from the pack to mark hidden sites. Faction outposts also offer daily intel when you are Known; notes are portable and one-shot.
Faction-held ground shows a coloured ring on the map once you have learned who runs it (outposts use the faction emblem).

hdb.title: Inside the block
bullets: Void decks open a side-elevation cutaway. Stairs stay visible even on sealed storeys; hover a reachable stair or door to preview the auto-path, then click — the pin walks hop by hop. Unvisited open floors stay fogged until you climb in. The roof is a short gated deck with extra loot; coming down checks every storey.

Sealed landings are gone for good. Corridor debris, barricades, and stair gates can be cleared (heat + time). A fob on a lanyard opens a matching grate quietly. Collapses are permanent — find another route.

Most loot doors are locked or barricaded. Pick a lock if you have a lockpick (quiet, consumed on the try); otherwise Force it and raise heat. Crowbar cheapens a smash. Room types each do one thing: search, a door trap, a live fire that burns per find, a nest or den fight, an empty shelter that dumps heat, a notice board, or a holdout service. Going down rolls Dexterity + Endurance once per storey — a fight stops you on that landing. Leave only from level 01.

tunnels.title: The tunnels
bullets: From an MRT platform, Plan tunnel travel opens the rail map. Pick a destination — default route is fewest intact stations. Some segments collapse each run: still passable, but a crawl through rubble and packs with no camps. Long trips may tempt the shortcut.

Confirming a route starts one crawl for the whole path. A station strip tracks the planned line, next stop, and transfers. You can exit at intermediate stations or keep walking to the far end. No surface range or weather underground. A heavy pack still wears you out; the walk itself is taxed less than the streets.

Between stations the running tunnel can split. Stay on the through line or peel into a side passage — it may run a few hops before it rejoins. Pick the node you can afford; the other way is gone once you step.

Camps offer a mat, a patch-up, or a swap — the only bunk underground. Obstructions vary: floodwater can hide a turned otter, falling debris wounds hard, a blackout eats the clock. Rare Contact is a Stalker that has been keeping pace. STA may toll the stairs down, and sometimes the bore itself.

evac.title: Evac
bullets: A map beacon marks the staging zone. Reach it during the timed window with a haul in your backpack (not stash or equipped). First press at the pad raises the channel — the crew reads this window's demand in numbers, and that read stays for the rest of the window. If the pack already clears, the same press pops the flare.

Fuel counts most, then meds and ammo; sealed water a little; food and scrap barely; weapons barely count as cargo. On the approach the radio vibe stays qualitative; only the pad channel names the quota. Boiling water burns fuel.
Miss the window and a new site opens after a cooldown — the horde keeps rising either way. Collapsed tunnels often force a detour toward the first beacon, or a high-risk crawl through the rubble.

score.title: Score
bullets: Score = (kills × 25 + carried loot value + days × 50) × day multiplier. Day 1 is ×1.0; each further day adds ×0.1.
A successful extract adds 2000 × the same day multiplier. Linger to climb the mult, then lift out late for the best board score.

Death still posts a score on this device, and to the worldwide board when you are online. Each extra day is worth more, but the horde front is heavier too — and when the island clock tops out at 100%, the city is overrun and the run ends.

kopi_o.name: Brew Kopi O
kopi_o.blurb: Coffee powder and water. It is plain, hot, and enough to keep moving.

kopi_sachet_drink.name: Mix Kopi Sachet
kopi_sachet_drink.blurb: One sachet and whatever water is safe enough to spare.

milo_drink.name: Mix Milo
milo_drink.blurb: Milo powder and water. Not fancy, but it puts something useful in you.

purify.name: Purify Water
purify.blurb: Tablets and twenty minutes turn a bottle of murk into something safe.

boil.name: Boil Water
boil.blurb: Slower than tablets and it costs you fuel — fuel also counts hard toward evac readiness.

bandages.name: Tear Dressings
bandages.blurb: Rags torn into strips. It will stop the bleeding — it will not stop what gets in afterwards.

spear_knife.name: Lash a Knife Spear
spear_knife.blurb: A kitchen knife taped to a length of timber. Keeps them at arm’s length.

spear_cleaver.name: Lash a Cleaver Spear
spear_cleaver.blurb: Heavier at the tip than a knife spear, and it bites deeper for it.

nail_bat.name: Drive Nails Through a Bat
nail_bat.blurb: Ugly, loud, and it tears more than it hits. The nails bend after a while.

cloth_wraps.name: Wrap Your Hands
cloth_wraps.blurb: Rag and tape over the knuckles. It is barely anything, and it is better than nothing.

shin_guards.name: Lash Shin Guards
shin_guards.blurb: Flat scrap padded with rag and taped to the shins. Legs are what they go for low.

scrap_shield.name: Lash a Scrap Shield
scrap_shield.blurb: Two sheets, a zip-tied handle, and an arm that will ache by evening.

padded_vest.name: Cut a Padded Vest
padded_vest.blurb: Foam soaks a bite better than it soaks a blade. You will miss it at bedtime.

scrap_helm.name: Beat Out a Scrap Helm
scrap_helm.blurb: A bucket of hammered plate with rag inside. You will not hear much coming.

scrap_armour.name: Rivet a Scrap Plate Vest
scrap_armour.blurb: Plate over rag over you. It stops teeth. It also announces every step you take.

tarp_poncho.name: Cut a Tarp Poncho
tarp_poncho.blurb: A head hole and taped seams. Dry and drab — but that tarp was your roof.

headlamp.name: Strap the Torch to Your Head
headlamp.blurb: The same light, and your off hand back. Worth an hour of fiddling with zip ties.

spear_parang.name: Lash a Parang Spear
spear_parang.blurb: The best of them — and it costs you the best blade you own.

parts.name: Strip for Parts
parts.blurb: Scrap is heavy and worth nothing. Parts are light and repair things.

shells.name: Reload Shells
shells.blurb: Handloading. Ugly, slow, and the only ammunition anyone still makes.

sleeping_bag.name: Stitch a Sleeping Bag
sleeping_bag.blurb: Rags and tape into something you can sleep in. Heavy, but better than the floor.

ez_link_knife.name: Laminate an EZ-Link Knife
ez_link_knife.blurb: Four spent cards and a scrap edge. STA will not take them as tribute anymore.

kopi_c.name: Brew Kopi C
kopi_c.blurb: Packet kopi, a squeeze of condensed milk, and the last of a bottle. It is not a kopitiam, but it is close.

cooked_mee.name: Cook Maggi
cooked_mee.blurb: A brick of noodles and a bottle of water. Heat is optional. Hunger is not.

milo_dinosaur.name: Mix a Milo Dinosaur
milo_dinosaur.blurb: The whole tin, extra powder on top, and whatever water you can spare. Heavy tin, light cup.

lockpick.name: Bend a Lockpick
lockpick.blurb: Two scraps bent into a rake and a tensioner. One door, maybe.

estate_kitchen.description: Thirty years of service, extra rice, and a stall the whole block still names.

estate_memory.name: Estate Memory
estate_memory.description: You already knew which blocks had the good stuff — and how many rooms were left.

operator.name: Operator
operator.description: Soft hands, sharp elbows, and a bag that always had one more pocket.

site_foreman.name: Site Foreman
site_foreman.description: You built these blocks. You know which walls hide what, and which ones come down.

made_man.name: Made Man
made_man.description: They know your face. The void decks are open ground. The checkpoints are not.

hypervigilant.name: Hypervigilant
hypervigilant.description: Training never lets you drop the watch. Sleep is a rumour.

shift_burnout.name: Shift Burnout
shift_burnout.description: Twelve-hour nights stacked until the tank never fills.

restlessness.name: Restlessness
restlessness.description: Still training for a race that is not coming. You cannot sit still, or quiet.

never_outdoors.name: Never Outdoors
never_outdoors.description: Lecture halls, malls, aircon. The island heat is a foreign country.
effects: +25% energy drain outdoors and in heat

stall_voice.name: Stall Voice
stall_voice.description: Everyone on the estate knows that voice. So does everything that hunts by sound.

ruined_knees.name: Ruined Knees
ruined_knees.description: Fourteenth storey, every day, for too many years. The stairs won.

desk_body.name: Desk Body
desk_body.description: Four reorgs, a return-to-office mandate, and no bus run since 2019.

heavy_hands.name: Heavy Hands
heavy_hands.description: You solve things by hitting them. Quiet was never the job.

warrant.name: Warrant
warrant.description: The Muster has a file. It is not flattering. Syndicate love is not free.

shadow_habit.name: Shadow Habit
shadow_habit.description: You learned which corridors stay quiet after midnight.

umbrella_city.name: Umbrella City
umbrella_city.description: You grew up walking through squalls with a folding umbrella and a dry bag.

haze_mask.name: Haze Habit
haze_mask.description: PSI days taught you to keep a mask and keep walking.

void_deck_chat.name: Void Deck Chat
void_deck_chat.description: You know how to open a conversation under fluorescent tubes.

train_memory.name: Train Memory
train_memory.description: Every interchange is still in your feet. The tunnels feel like a second street.

sharp_eye.name: Sharp Eye
sharp_eye.description: You notice the wrong shadow before it notices you.

mall_rat.name: Mall Rat
mall_rat.description: Aircon atriums were your outdoors. Real weather still feels wrong.

tone_deaf.name: Tone Deaf
tone_deaf.description: You say the wrong thing at the wrong door.

loud_soles.name: Loud Soles
loud_soles.description: Hard heels, hard habits. Everything hears you coming.

lost_without_maps.name: Lost Without Maps
lost_without_maps.description: Without a pin on your phone you still turn the wrong way at every junction.

faction_checkpoint.title: {short} Gate

lines.payEmpty: Empty hands. They shrug, not unkindly, and point you back the way you came.
lines.leave: You step back from the table. They don't follow.

tell: There's a table across the entrance, and someone sitting at it.
Someone raises a hand as you approach — not a weapon. A hand.
A ledger sits open on a crate by the door of {name}.
They've put a stool in the doorway. That's the whole gate.
text: {faction} keeps a book at {name}. "{tribute} gets you on the grounds — and your name in the right column."
The one on the gate at {name} taps the open page. "Entrance fee. One {tribute}. Then we know you."
A {short} volunteer looks you over from behind a folding table. "Don't know your face. One {tribute} for the register and you can go in."
"Sign in," says the gate. "One {tribute}. Or turn around."
night: A lamp over the ledger at {name}. "{short}. One {tribute} and you're on the list."
wet: They've pulled the table under the awning. "{tribute} and you can come in out of this."

faction_shakedown.title: {short} Tribute

lines.payEmpty: Empty hands buy nothing. They turn you around.
lines.leave: You leave before tribute becomes blood.

tell: Voices inside — not the dead. The dead don't chat.
Someone whistles once as you reach the entrance. A signal.
There's a mark sprayed by the door, still tacky.
A shape peels off the wall ahead of you.
text: {faction} blockers fill the doorway of {name}. "Tribute. One {tribute}. Then maybe we talk."
Two of {faction}'s people are already inside {name}, and they saw you first. "One {tribute} — for the damage."
One of {faction}'s lookouts drops down off the ledge, hand out. "You owe us. One {tribute}."
{faction} has {name} sewn up. The one doing the talking taps a crowbar against her boot. "{tribute}. Repair what you broke."
Someone in {short} colours blocks the entrance without hurrying about it. "Nothing personal. One {tribute}."
night: A torch beam pins you in the doorway of {name}. "{short}. One {tribute}, and lower your hands."
They let you get all the way to the entrance before the lights come on. "One {tribute}, and we forget you came at night."
wet: {faction} has the entrance to {name} tarped over and manned. "Dry inside. One {tribute}."

locked_door.title: Locked Security Door

lines.pickFailTime: You work the lock until your hands cramp. It doesn't give.
lines.findOk: You circle the building and find a service door nobody thought about.
lines.findFailTime: You circle the whole building for nothing.
lines.findFailEnergy: The circuit costs you. Legs heavy, nothing gained.
lines.findFailDeny: No way in but the hard way, and not today.

tell: The main way in is shut, and shut properly.
Someone secured this place before they left.
The doors have been chained from the inside.
text: A steel security door bars the way into {name}. It can be forced — loudly.
The roller shutter on {name} is down and padlocked. Whoever locked it didn't come back out.
Fire door, magnetic lock, dead building. {name} is sealed and it doesn't care how badly you need it.
Someone welded a bar across the entrance to {name}. Thorough. Inconvenient.
The doors to {name} are chained. Through the gap you can see shelves — and they look untouched.
night: In the dark you can barely find the seam of the security door at {name}, let alone the lock.
wet: The shutter on {name} is streaked with rain and locked fast. Every sound you make here will carry.

desperate_survivor.title: The Desperate Survivor

choices.give: Give 1× Bottled Water, Isotonic Drink or Canned Food

tell: Someone is sheltering just inside the entrance.
You're not the first one to want in here today.
A cough, close by. Human.
text: A gaunt figure is huddled inside the doorway of {name}. "Please… you got water?"
Someone has made a nest of cardboard just inside {name}. She doesn't get up. "Just a bottle, boss. Anything."
A man steps out of the stairwell with both hands showing, eyeing your pack. "Two days no drink already."
There's a kid's school bag by the entrance to {name}, and the man wearing it hasn't eaten in a while. "Spare something?"
Someone blocks your way into {name} — not with a weapon, just with need. "You look like you're doing okay, ah."
night: A voice out of the dark inside {name}, cracked and dry. "Don't shine that at me. Please. You got water?"
wet: Someone is pressed into the doorway of {name} out of the rain, soaked through anyway. "Water? Clean water, I mean."

rival_scavenger.title: Someone Got Here First

choices.race: Race them for the back rooms
choices.watch: Hang back and read the place

lines.raceWin: You get there first, and you're winded for it.
lines.raceLose: They know the floor better than you do. By the time you reach the back, it's bare.
lines.split: You each take a half and work it in silence. It's almost companionable.
lines.watchWin: You wait them out from the stairwell and learn the building for free.
lines.watchLose: You wait them out and learn nothing except that your legs hurt.

tell: Fresh boot prints in the dust, going in. None coming out.
Something falls over inside, and someone swears.
A trolley is wedged in the doorway to hold it open.
text: Someone else is already working {name} — you can hear them stripping a shelf. They haven't seen you yet.
A scavenger in a motorcycle helmet is halfway through {name}, bags at her feet. She looks up. Neither of you moves.
There's another survivor inside {name}, filling a duffel fast. Whoever commits first gets the back rooms.
You aren't the only one who thought of {name} today. He raises a hand — not a weapon, just a hand.
night: A torch is sweeping the aisles of {name}, and it isn't yours. Whoever holds it is working fast.

armed_raider.title: Armed Claim

lines.bluffOk: You sell a story about a bigger crew coming. They clear a lane.

tell: Someone is posted at the entrance like they own it.
A rifle sling creaks. Whoever's inside is not scavenging quietly.
Fresh brass on the step. Recent work.
text: A raider has claimed the doorway of {name}, kit stacked behind him. "Walk away, or pay in blood."
Someone with a parang and a stolen vest is screening {name}. He's already decided you're competition.
An armed crew of one is stripping {name} methodically. He looks up mid-cut and doesn't bother with a greeting.
The entrance to {name} is blocked by someone who treats looting like a job with overtime.
night: A red laser dots the frame of {name} for half a second, then vanishes. Someone is hunting this block.

block_tout.title: Doorway Tax

lines.leave: You leave him his cardboard throne.

tell: Someone is hanging around the entrance like it's theirs to tax.
A voice calls out before you reach the door — friendly, too friendly.
There's a folding stool by the doorway. Occupied.
text: A tout at {name} opens with a smile and a price. "Entry fee, ah. Small one. Or we have a problem."
Someone has set up shop in the doorway of {name} — no badge, just nerve. "You want in, you talk to me."
A block tout blocks {name} with nothing but attitude and a scrap of cardboard that says ENTRY. He means it.
He's not a guard and not a scavenger — just a man charging for the privilege of walking into {name}.
night: A cigarette tip glows in the doorway of {name}. "Night rate," someone says. "Still cheap."

rigged_door.title: The Door Is Rigged

choices.disarm: Trace the wire and disarm it
choices.power: Work out what it's tied to
choices.around: Go the long way round (slow, safe)

lines.disarmFailWound: The frame comes apart with a bang and takes a piece of you with it.
lines.disarmFailZombies: Every dead thing on the block heard that.
lines.powerOk: You follow the line back, find the anchor, and pull it slack.
lines.powerFailTime: You lose half an hour to a puzzle you can't solve.
lines.powerFailDeny: Not worth losing a hand over.
lines.aroundTime: You give the door a wide berth and let yourself in through a window on the far side.
lines.aroundEnergy: The long way round leaves you winded — but in.
lines.leave: You back out the way you came.

tell: There's something wrong with how this door sits.
A thin line of fishing wire catches the light.
Someone left this place ready for visitors.
text: The entrance to {name} has been rigged — wire at ankle height, and a bundle of something taped behind the frame.
Whoever held {name} last booby-trapped the way in and never came back to disarm it.
A tripwire runs across the doorway of {name}, strung to a cluster of tins. Not lethal. Very loud.
{name} has been made unfriendly on purpose: broken glass set in the frame, and a line running somewhere you can't see.
wet: Rain has soaked the rigging on the door of {name}, but the wire is still taut.

quiet_tap.title: The Tap Still Runs

choices.queue: Take your place in the queue

lines.queue: You wait your turn like everyone else. It takes an hour and nobody thanks you for it.
lines.tradeEmpty: You've nothing to trade, and they've nothing spare for you.
lines.leave: You leave the queue to its water and move on.

tell: You can hear running water. Actual running water.
There's a queue. An orderly one.
People are here, and none of them are panicking.
text: A standpipe behind {name} is still pressurised, and eleven people are queuing at it in the shade. Nobody is pushing.
Someone has rigged a working tap at {name} and made a system of it — a queue, a tally, a woman with a clipboard.
There's clean water at {name}, and a line of survivors waiting their turn for it. They watch you decide what kind of person you are.
night: A single lamp over a working tap at {name}, and a short, patient queue beneath it.

body_in_the_doorway.title: Body in the Doorway

choices.step: Step over and get on with it

lines.stripFailZombies: The body comes free all at once, and the clatter carries.
lines.readOk: Bite on the forearm, defensive. Whatever did it went back inside.
lines.readFail: You learn nothing except that you didn't want to look that closely.

tell: Something is lying across the threshold.
The smell reaches you before the doorway does.
Flies. A lot of them, and all in one place.
text: A body is slumped in the entrance to {name}, pack still on. It has been there a while, and it is wedged.
Someone died in the doorway of {name} with their kit on. Moving them means touching them.
There's a corpse across the way into {name} — recent enough to still be carrying, old enough to be part of the floor.
wet: A body lies in the flooded entrance to {name}, pack half-submerged. The water has not been kind.

looters_fleeing.title: Wrong-Way Traffic

choices.chase: Chase them — grab what they dropped

lines.chaseLose: They know the floor better. You arrive winded and empty-handed.
lines.readOk: You clock the route they took and what they skipped.
lines.readFail: They're gone before you learn anything useful.

tell: Someone bursts out of the entrance — wrong way, wrong speed.
A crash inside, then footsteps coming at you.
The door swings open and someone nearly runs you down.
You hear a bag hit the floor, then someone cursing their way out.
text: A scavenger bolts out of {name} with both arms full and nearly bowls you over. Whatever they grabbed is still in the building.
Someone tears past you out of {name}, kit bouncing. The back rooms might still have something.
A figure stumbles out of {name} clutching a duffel — they saw you too late to stop.
Wrong-way traffic at {name}: someone exits at a sprint, leaving the place open behind them.
night: A torch beam swings out of {name} and someone runs without looking. The door stays open.

smoke_block.title: Smoke Under the Door

choices.side: Find a side entry out of the smoke

lines.sideOk: You circle to a service door where the air is clear enough.
lines.sideFailTime: Every way in is the same haze.
lines.sideFailDeny: Not worth coughing your lungs out today.
lines.pushFailWound: You stumble in the haze and catch something sharp on the way down.
lines.pushFailDeny: You back out coughing blood and ash.
lines.wait: You wait downwind until the smoke thins enough to breathe.
lines.leave: You leave the smoke to its work.

tell: Smoke curls out from under the door.
The air at the entrance tastes of burnt plastic.
Something inside is still smouldering.
You cough before you reach the handle.
text: Smoke pours from the entrance to {name}. Something burned in there and never quite stopped.
The doorway of {name} is hazy with smoke — not a bonfire, a kitchen or a stall gone wrong.
You can barely see the frame of {name} through the smoke. It might clear. It might not.
Burnt oil and charred plastic hang in the air at {name}. Going in blind is a bad idea.
night: An orange glow flickers behind the smoke at {name}. Still hot in there.
wet: Rain damps the smoke at {name} but the air inside is still wrong.

distress_beacon.title: Still Broadcasting

choices.trace: Trace the signal — read the place
choices.ignore: Ignore it and go in quiet

lines.traceOk: The message tells you more about the building than the broadcaster meant.
lines.traceFail: Static and repetition. You learn nothing but the clock.
lines.rushZombies: The beacon was bait — or the dead answered it first.

tell: A radio crackles somewhere inside — on a loop.
You hear a recorded message, tinny and repeating.
Someone left a beacon running. It hasn't been switched off.
A siren wails once, then a voice on a speaker.
text: A distress beacon is still broadcasting from inside {name}. "…anyone receiving… coordinates…"
A PA system at {name} loops a pre-recorded SOS. Someone wanted to be found.
The radio desk at {name} is still transmitting. Static, then a voice, then static again.
An emergency beacon at {name} hasn't given up yet. The message repeats every thirty seconds.
night: In the dark the beacon at {name} is the only thing still working.
wet: Rain drums the roof while the beacon at {name} keeps calling.

nomad_trader.title: Travelling Merchant

lines.tradeEmpty: No food, no trade. They fold the mat and let you pass anyway.
lines.leave: You leave the trader to their stock.

tell: Someone has set up a mat by the entrance — not scavenging, trading.
A pack is open on the step. Someone is counting stock.
There's a handwritten price list taped to the doorframe.
You smell cooking oil and hear someone haggling with nobody.
text: A travelling merchant has camped the entrance to {name}. "Trade only. I don't bite unless you do."
Someone has turned the doorway of {name} into a stall — small stock, fair prices, no questions.
A nomad trader spreads goods on a tarp at {name}. "Food for medicine. Batteries for tins. You pick."
The entrance to {name} smells of someone else's cooking. They've got a mat, a scale, and a smile that doesn't reach their eyes.
night: A lamp over a travelling trader at {name}. "Night rate's the same. Food talks."

car_blockade.title: Abandoned Barricade

choices.shift: Shift a car enough to squeeze through
choices.gap: Find a gap between the wrecks

lines.shiftOk: Metal groans and your shoulders pay for every inch.
lines.shiftFailEnergy: The car doesn't budge. Your arms do, and not in a good way.
lines.gapFailTime: You walk the whole barricade looking for a seam.
lines.longTime: You circle the block and come in through the loading bay.
lines.longEnergy: The long way round leaves you winded — but in.
lines.leave: You leave the barricade where it is.

tell: Abandoned cars choke the entrance.
Someone lined vehicles across the way in — bumper to bumper.
The driveway is a parking lot nobody can leave.
Tyres and metal block the only way in.
text: Abandoned cars barricade the entrance to {name} — bumper to bumper, keys gone, doors locked.
Someone pushed three vehicles across the way into {name} and walked away.
The forecourt of {name} is a junk barrier of stalled cars. There might be a gap if you look.
A barricade of abandoned vehicles blocks {name}. Thorough. Not impassable.
night: In the dark the car barricade at {name} is just shapes and metal.
wet: Rain slicks the bonnets blocking {name}. Every surface is slippery.

flooded_entry.title: Knee-Deep at the Door

lines.wadeOk: You pick a line where the footing is still there under the water.
lines.wadeFailTime: The water hides a step and you go in hard.
lines.wadeFailWound: Something sharp under the water finds your leg.
lines.rushEnergy: Cold water to the knee and every step a fight.
lines.rushWound: You misstep on something that used to be a floor tile.
lines.leave: You leave the flood to settle.

tell: Water pours out when you push the door.
The entrance is ankle-deep and rising.
Someone's sandbags didn't hold.
You hear water moving inside before you see it.
text: The entrance to {name} is knee-deep in floodwater — drain runoff, or something worse backed up inside.
Monsoon water has pooled at {name} and nobody drained it. The way in is a wade.
A blocked drain turned the doorway of {name} into a wading pool. The shelves might still be dry.
Floodwater fills the lobby of {name}. Whatever's worth taking is above the waterline — if you can reach it.
wet: The rain hasn't stopped and neither has the water at {name}. It's worse than yesterday.

mrt_toll.title: STA Turnstile Toll
mrt_toll.text: An STA marshal has the gate chained at waist height. "Tunnel's not free. Cells, a torch, a tin — I'm not fussy. One of them and you're through."

lines.payEmpty: No fare, no tunnel. You take the stairs back up.

field_doctor.title: Field Doctor
field_doctor.tell: Someone is running a clinic out of a unit in {name}.
text: A woman in a stained polo waves you onto a camp mat. "I can clean and pack that. I don't take money — I take food. One tin, one meal, whatever you have."
The unit smells of iodine. "Sit," says the man sorting gauze by the window. "An hour of my time for something to eat. That's the whole price list."
Someone has taped a red cross to the gate of this unit. "Food first," they say, without looking up. "Then I'll look at you."

lines.treatTime: You lie still while they work.
lines.treat: The field doctor patches you up. Clean dressings, tight and even.
lines.payEmpty: The doctor wants payment in food. You have none to give.
lines.leave: You keep your food and your wounds. The gate closes behind you.

tell: A folding table, a ledger, and someone who still stands like they're on duty.
A clipboard comes up as you approach — not a rifle. A clipboard.
They've chalked a queue line on the ground in front of {name}.
text: The Muster keeps a book at {name}. "Name in the right column. One {tribute}. Then we know you."
An NSman in mixed kit looks you over. "Managed order. One {tribute} for the register."
"Have you served?" The ledger is already open. "One {tribute} either way."
night: A lamp over the ledger at {name}. "Muster. One {tribute} and you're on the list."
wet: They've pulled the table under the school porch. "{tribute} and you can come in out of this."

tell: Steam, a queue, and someone with a ladle who is also the gate.
A plastic stool in the doorway of {name}. The auntie on it is not moving.
They've strung a rope across the wet-market entrance. People are waiting anyway.
text: Gotong Royong holds {name}. "Eat first, then we talk. One {tribute} for the pot."
A stallholder wipes her hands. "We pool what we have. One {tribute} and you can come in."
"This is neighbours' food. One {tribute}. Don't bring trouble to the table."
night: A pot still going at {name}. "Gotong. One {tribute} and you're fed after."
wet: They've pulled the queue under the tarpaulin. "{tribute} and you can come in out of this."

tell: A chain at waist height across the unpaid side of the gate.
Someone in a high-vis vest that used to mean something is sitting on the turnstile.
The barrier at {name} is down. A marshal is the only thing moving.
text: STA has the gate at {name} chained. "Tunnel's not free. One {tribute}."
A marshal taps the turnstile. "Fare. One {tribute}. Then you can go down."
"Platform's manned. One {tribute} and you're through."
night: A torch beam off the tiles at {name}. "STA. One {tribute} and you can go down."
wet: Rain drums the concourse. "{tribute} and you can come in out of this — the stairs stay dry."

tell: The whistle is friendlier than last time. Still a whistle.
Someone at {name} nods you toward the stool.
text: The 88 have a book of their own at {name}. "You're on it. One {tribute} anyway."
A runner at the void deck of {name} holds out a palm. "Known is not free. One {tribute}."

tell: A whistle from the void deck. Not a bird.
Someone peels off a pillar at {name}, unhurried.
There's a mark sprayed by the door, still tacky.
text: 88 blockers fill the doorway of {name}. "Tribute. One {tribute}. Then maybe we talk."
Two of the Syndicate are already inside {name}. "One {tribute} — for the damage."
A lookout drops down off the ledge, hand out. "You owe the decks. One {tribute}."
night: A torch beam pins you in the doorway of {name}. "88. One {tribute}, and lower your hands."
wet: They've tarped the entrance. "Dry inside. One {tribute}."
